result.rationale: The diff shows parseRefreshTokenResponse returns `refreshTokenResponse` (the full zod safeParse result object, not `.data`), and in GoogleCalendarService the line `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` followed by `data: { key }` in the prisma.credential.update stores that envelope directly as credential.key, replacing the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` payload. This corrupts stored credentials with a {success, data} wrapper, breaking subsequent reads.

judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full zod safeParse envelope ({success, data}) instead of .data, and GoogleCalendarService stores that envelope directly as credential.key, replacing the previously stored googleCredentialSchema.parse() payload. On the first token refresh after deploy, every Google Calendar user's stored credential becomes {success:true, data:{...}} (in the default non-sharing configuration), so the next read of credential.key finds refresh_token/access_token undefined and Google Calendar sync permanently fails until the user reinstalls the app.

On the first token refresh after deploy, every Google Calendar user's stored credential becomes {success:true, data:{...}} (in the default non-sharing configuration), so the next read of credential.key finds refresh_token/access_token undefined and Google Calendar sync permanently fails until the user reinstalls the app.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (the `{ success, data, error }` envelope), not `...data`. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh path was changed from `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (which returns the parsed payload) to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists `data: { key }` to Prisma. That will store the envelope into `credential.key` rather than the credential fields themselves, breaking subsequent reads that expect `credential.key.refresh_token/access_token/...`.
